surface_scope_note: The listed pre-surface cases explicitly select built-in filesystem and retain their stated layout fixtures. Cases 7–8 cover external memory and executive-journal patch operations. See README.md for actual code/test/confirmation/handoff evidence.

evals.name: free-standing-accepted-implicit
evals.prompt: bump requests from 2.31 to 2.32 in the manifest

context.invocation: implicit — routing rule classifies a small contained change; there is no /fast command

expected_output: Routing triggered fast implicitly — the lane activated without any slash command
Shared triage (conduct/references/triage.md, default+floor inline) confirmed the bump touches only the manifest
Change applied to the dependency manifest only
Quality Gate run after the change
Nothing written to .ai/work/ (free-standing writes no executive artifacts)
A conventional-commit message suggested (chore(deps): ...), not executed
One-line recap given in chat

evals.name: too-complex-routes-into-chain
evals.prompt: quick change: update the requests package to version 5

context.simulated_blast_radius: 23 call sites across 9 modules, a custom requests.Session subclass whose signature changes, adapter/retry config moves to a new API

expected_output: Agent investigated blast radius before editing (counted call sites, detected contract + migration impact)
Shared triage scored the work above inline (design at least) — fast refused to execute it
No partial change applied; worktree left untouched
Refusal was concrete (named file/call-site count and the changed contract), not just 'too complex'
Agent routed the developer into the conduct chain, carrying the triage evidence and depth so it isn't re-derived from scratch

evals.name: plan-adjustment-with-confirmation
evals.prompt: add an email format validation to the invitation endpoint, it was not in the plan

work_files.tasks.md: Phase 2 (invitation service) in progress, tasks T-005..T-008

expected_output: Agent triaged the change as inline (one serializer + one test, contained)
Agent recognized the change as a plan adjustment (in scope of the active plan)
Dirty worktree treated as expected mid-phase, not as a blocking surprise
Behavioral change with TDD enabled: a test was added/adjusted and passes
Quality Gate run green
Agent executed the change THEN asked the developer to confirm correctness BEFORE writing executive artifacts
On confirmation: tasks.md got a new checked task with the next free T-NNN id (no renumbering), tagged (fast, <date>); plan.md got a Plan amendments bullet; walkthrough.md got the out-of-band block
Agent did not advance the plan itself; suggested a commit without running it

evals.name: big-out-of-band-fold-or-park
evals.prompt: we also need to add SSO login with Azure AD, can you slip that in while we're at it?

context.simulated_blast_radius: new auth flow, new external integration, settings + middleware + user model — clearly design/spec depth

expected_output: Agent triaged the request as far above inline while a plan is active
Did NOT touch code and did NOT create a second plan silently

Surfaced the size with evidence and offered exactly two exits: fold it into the active plan as a new phase (via the conduct chain, with a dated amendment) or park-and-replan (pause at the last reversible checkpoint, re-enter the chain)
Waited for the developer's choice; the active plan.md was not overwritten or drifted
Whichever exit is chosen, the folding/replanning itself belongs to conduct — fast only surfaced and routed

evals.name: borderline-asks-developer
evals.prompt: small change: extract the pricing calculation logic to its own module and update the imports

context.simulated_blast_radius: ambiguous — could be 2 files or could ripple through ~8 importers

expected_output: Agent investigated before deciding (located the pricing logic and counted importers)
Agent surfaced its blast-radius estimate to the developer rather than deciding silently
Agent offered the choice: proceed as inline vs. enter the conduct chain, and waited for the decision
No code changed before the developer chose

evals.name: uninstrumented-project-still-executes
evals.prompt: bump lodash from 4.17.20 to 4.17.21 in package.json

context.skill_install: global (~/.claude/skills/), project has never used JAIBA
context.repo_state: no AGENTS.md (or one unrelated to JAIBA), no .ai/ directory
context.ci_facts: package.json has a `test` script; CI workflow runs `npm test`

expected_output: Agent ran the brain check, found no JAIBA marker / brain (neither concept bundle nor legacy flat), but did NOT block the change
Triaged scope normally (single dependency bump, contained)
Treated the change as free-standing — did not look for an active plan

Quality Gate fallback used the repo's own package.json `test` script / CI command, not a brain-defined Phase Gate (no `quality-gate` concept or `constitution.md §6` exists — this project isn't instrumented)
Change applied to package.json (and lockfile if present)
Closing recap mentioned jaiba-init once as an opportunity, without making it a precondition for the change
Nothing written to .ai/work/

evals.name: external-inline-code-change-hands-off-after-confirmation
evals.prompt: Change the inline tax calculation to round to two decimal places.

context.ownership: exact project ID and context ID resolved; one authorized writer
context.plan: approved, executing; tax calculation is adjacent to its scope
context.developer_protocol: after the tested code change, developer first refuses confirmation in one run; confirms in another
context.failure_scenario: simulated executive revision conflict on conduct handoff

expected_output: Triage classifies the contained code change inline; the code diff is delegated to a callable executor while fast still owns the amendment, exercising test/Quality Gate before seeking confirmation
On refusal it makes no executive memory write; on confirmation it hands proposed task/amendment/walkthrough updates and captured full-read revisions to conduct
Fast never writes JAIBA executive objects itself; conduct compares revisions and verifies full readback
On simulated revision conflict, conduct stops and does not claim a successful update or retry blindly
The fake backend trace is simulation, not proof of actual Engram or unseen library behavior

evals.name: plan-adjustment-executive-journal-patch
evals.prompt: add a rate limit validation to the login endpoint, it was not in the plan

context.selected_surface: external record-store surface with executive-journal capability (1.1.0)
context.code_change: contained inline validation in login handler with test

expected_output: Triaged code change as inline and verified tests and Quality Gate pass
Executed code change then obtained developer confirmation before touching executive artifacts
On confirmation on a surface with executive-journal capability (MSV-005), emits surgical patch operations rather than monolithic object rewrites
Emits add-task to append the new checked task with next free T-NNN ID to tasks
Emits append-to-section (or append-section) on plan for Plan amendments bullet and on walkthrough for the out-of-band record
Supplies expected-head revision from last verified render to guarantee single-writer consistency
Conduct verifies full readback and updates context-head slot, achieving O(delta) mutation efficiency

evals.name: delegation-with-inline-fallback
evals.prompt: quick fix: add null check to user display name in the profile component

context.executor_status: callable in primary run; unavailable / not callable in fallback scenario

expected_output: An inline code change is delegated to a callable executor (executor-low, executor-medium, or executor-high matching the change load)
Executor receives the change, allowed files, and gate commands with instructions not to write executive memory
Fast remains the only writer of the amendment; the executor does not write executive memory
If no executor is callable, fast alerts with the role and the concrete blocker (missing, not callable, or misconfigured)
After the alert, fast does the change inline and does not block

evals.name: unnamed-amendment-enters-fast
evals.prompt: add a timeout configuration parameter to the webhook client call

context.prompt_phrasing: change request outside current planned tasks without mentioning fast

expected_output: Active plan exists and the message is a change outside the current tasks that does not say fast
The change request still enters fast via the implicit routing rule
Fast triages the out-of-band change as inline and delegates the code change to a callable executor
Fast remains the only writer of the amendment, confirming with the developer before updating work artifacts

evals.name: continue-does-not-enter-fast
expected_output: Prompt is 'continue' while an active approved plan exists
Request stays on conduct execute; fast does not take it
Routing rule does not trigger fast on continuation cues (continue / next / go)
